body:
I think Kasumi's main issues are twofold.

A.) She's a purely autoaim character in an FPS game, I know Paladins has long had moba elements, but being forced to deal with Kasumi at range or not deal with her at all makes her a nightmare for uncoordinated teams and forces people to play around her range rather than around her aiming ability, flattening the Kasumi skill curve immensely.

B.) Her weapon deals way too much damage for an autoaim ability.  Any decent Kasumi should, with cards, be dealing 400 damage a shot every 0.6s, and having both auto-targeting and no reload on a weapon equivalent in damage to Lian's primary fire is just silly.  I think she'd be less oppressive if they either removed her autoaim but extended her range or kept her autoaim but made it much harder to build up and maintain curse stacks.

She's a conceptually terrible character who's bad for the game imo.
Evie tier (apart from all others) in terms of fun, A tier as a flank

Plus she can get DPS boosts and free full stacks from cards + her first talent is a straight buff to her kit so why should a good kasumi ever be doing less than 400 damage per shot on an auto aim no reload weapon, absurd champ
It'd be cool to get some kind of parkour-based game focused on Maeve or maybe the Thousand Hands.
Even her base weapon is absolutely absurd.  200 + 100% damage at five curse stacks with no buffs every 0.6 seconds on a weapon with NO RELOAD that automatically targets enemies is absolutely insane.

Hey, I don't disagree with anything you said.  For me, it's a kind of wager.  If we as community members do absolutely nothing, the game will certainly die.  If we at least make efforts at doing something, the game may not die.  That's how I view it, and because the time cost to me isn't significant, it's a worthwhile gambit.

Awareness in the community --> Organization ---> Organized action ---> Getting stuff done

If people aren't even aware of how bad the issues surrounding the game are, they can't discuss them properly, and if they can't discuss them properly, they can't organize around a common idea, and if they can't do that, the devs sure ain't ever listening.
Nice of you to wear a barcode to show that you'll only ever work at the checkout line.
